messages:
lina: Hey team — customer reported our support API routed a refund request to create_credit (gift card) instead of issue_refund. Happened twice this morning for different customers. Request ID: r_1a2b3c. Can someone triage? @raj

support-bot: Ticket INC-4219 opened for r_1a2b3c (assigned to support on-call). Metadata: region=us-east, model=router-v4, heur=default.

raj: Thanks, looking. Do you have the raw request body and the router debug snippet? Also which model & routing policy was used?

lina: Pasting minimal repro (redacted):
```json
{
  "customer_id": "cus_ABC123",
  "action": "refund",
  "amount": 2500,
  "currency": "USD",
  "reason": "return - defective",
  "source": "card_XXX"
}
```
Router debug (log excerpt):
```
[router-v4] candidate_scores: {"create_credit":0.62, "issue_refund":0.58, "create_note":0.12}
selected: create_credit (score 0.62)
signature_match(create_credit): amount: optional int, currency: optional str
signature_match(issue_refund): amount: required int, currency: required str
confidence_delta: 0.04
```
lina: The caller used our support API endpoint (/v1/support/actions) — no explicit tool field in payload. Expect issue_refund. Customer-facing result was a gift card credit.

raj: Hmm — scores are close. Router favored create_credit because its signature is more permissive (amount optional). That small delta should normally fall through to tie-breaker (priority table) but looks like priority is equal. Any recent model or signature changes?

chris: Quick mitigation: bump issue_refund priority in routing table for support channel, or set a tie-breaker to prefer tools with "refund" intent on explicit action=="refund". We can hotfix in config for next deploy window.

lina: Can you confirm whether we can match on the top-level field action=="refund"? The autorouter currently only uses the prompt + json body signatures.

raj: We don't currently include explicit top-level action field in signature scoring. Two options: 1) update scoring to treat top-level action fields as strong intent signals (short-term), 2) make create_credit signature stricter (require giftcard_id or voucher_code) so it won't catch refunds. Both are safe.

chris: I can push a quick signature tightening for create_credit (require gift_card_id) — that reduces false positives and has low blast radius. I'll prepare a change and a canary.

lina: Thanks. Also customer impacted count: 3 in last 24h. They'll need manual reversal for gift card + actual refund issuance. I'll coordinate with ops for make-whole.

raj: Follow-up: let's also add a small test to our eval suite — prompt+payload variations where amount is present but intent=refund should score issue_refund > create_credit by at least 0.15. I'll add an eval case.

chris: Deploy plan: push signature change to router-config v2026-03-17a -> canary us-east -> monitor autoroute_misroute rate for 1h. If green, roll. ETA 30m.

lina: Great. One more ask: can we log the exact candidate payload passed to tool for 30m so we can backtrace any other misroutes?

raj: Good call. I'll enable verbose candidate logging for that ticket id for 2 hours.

lina: Awesome. Marking INC-4219 as triaged. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: INC-4219 updated: assignee=chris, status=triaged, labels=misroute,refund,hotfix

chris: Starting signature change now. Will post results in this thread.

(7 minutes later)

chris: Canary deployed. Initial telemetry: misroute_rate for refund-intent down from 0.7% -> 0.03% in canary. No regressions observed so far.

raj: I'll add the eval and a regression alert to catch future signature relaxations.

lina: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with ops on customer reimbursements and close once manual fixes are applied.
